items.title: Direct summands of sums of quotients of the ring by principal ideals, characterized by a lifting property for short exact sequences
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes the modules that are direct summands of direct sums of quotients of the ring by principal ideals as those for which maps out of the module lift along every short exact sequence whose submodule is divisible by every element in the strong sense that the intersection of the submodule with the multiples of an element equals the multiples of the submodule (statement lines 37585-37598). The first implication is an explicit lift obtained from that divisibility, while the converse builds the canonical presentation of the module as a cokernel indexed by the pairs of an element and a map out of the corresponding quotient, and then verifies the divisibility hypothesis by correcting a coefficient tuple using the vanishing of the combination (proof lines 37600-37635). The construction of the canonical presentation and the correction step are the substance of the argument. The counted statement contains the author's own reference environment, which the retained preamble typesets as a comment, so the citation inside it is discarded and no bibliography is needed; the counted span contains no cross reference, so the card carries no navigation stub.
